probe: Both annual reports searched for a demographic breakdown; neither publishes one. The application does not ask.
No income data appears in either report. EFA eligibility has never been means-tested, so the program does not gather it.
Both PDFs searched for a grade-level participation breakdown; neither publishes one. Only eligibility-category, schooling-sector and prior-school-status breakdowns exist.

The 2023-24 report lists a city for every participating school; the 2024-25 report's Table 1 omits city for about 83% of rows, keeping it only to disambiguate same-named campuses. No report has ever given participants' own district or county.

citation: 2023-24 annual report, complete text (28 pp.): the 15 dollar amounts it prints appear on pp. 5, 7, 22, 23 and 24, and none is per-school.
probe: The 2023-24 report contains 15 dollar amounts in 28 pages, on pages 5, 7, 22, 23 and 24. None is per-school. Year-on-year growth in money received by a named school cannot be read from these reports at all.

probe: No 2025-26 annual report exists yet (expected ~October 2026), and no interim per-school expenditure release was found.
Neither annual report publishes tuition. The state collects it on the school application form.
obtained_by: The Arkansas Advocate obtained 170 application packets under FOIA and reported an average tuition of about $9,800 for 2026-27 (1 July 2026). The figure on this page is theirs; the underlying records are the state's.

probe: The reports publish category totals and a recipient appendix, never the transactions themselves. The payment platform holds them.
6,495 applied and 5,700 were approved in 2023-24; 18,921 applied and 14,457 were approved in 2024-25. Nothing published explains a single denial.
No service-level or processing-time figure appears in either report, despite a vendor backlog documented by KATV on 1 July 2026 (41,000 pending requests; a 25-day target against delays reaching 45).
The program collects a norm-referenced test score and nothing else about a participating student's schooling.

A complete enumeration of the Arkansas General Assembly's document server over 2023-03-01 to 2026-07-27 — 7,232 index rows, 5,932 attachments, 663 meetings, all HTTP 200, zero failures — found exactly two EFA reports filed to the legislature in 41 months, and no quarterly series. Agendas in the same window carry 171 genuine quarterly filings from other agencies, so a DESE quarterly would have appeared in the index had one been filed.
No 2025-26 annual report exists on the DESE site or the legislative server. The only 2025-26 figures in the record are the 2024-25 report's forward-looking Outlook paragraph and its retention table.

No state publication held by this project contains 2026-27 participation counts: not the two annual reports, not the appropriation acts, not the DESE program pages, not the legislative exhibit server.
obtained_by: The Arkansas Advocate published approved counts attributed to the Department (51,041 approved — 28,096 private school, 22,945 homeschool, as of 26 June 2026) alongside school-application figures from records obtained under FOIA.
